groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: A person may not practice, attempt to practice, or offer to practice optometry without first obtaining a license from the board.

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.value: Board of Examiners in Optometry
example.quote: There is created the Board of Examiners in Optometry to regulate and control the practice of optometry

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.value: Board of Examiners in Optometry
example.quote: There is created the Board of Examiners in Optometry to regulate and control the practice of optometry

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.value: standalone_board
example.quote: There is created the Board of Examiners in Optometry to regulate and control the practice of optometry and to protect and promote the public health, welfare, and safety.

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.

example.quote: Every person desiring to practice optometry in this state shall be 19 years of age, or over

fields.meaning: Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.

example.quote: Every person desiring to practice optometry in this state shall be 19 years of age, or over, a citizen of the United States or, if not a citizen of the United States, a person who is legally present i

fields.meaning: Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board
example.quote: shall be a graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board

example.value: American Optometric Association
example.quote: "recognized school or college of optometry" means a school or college approved by the American Optometric Association or a committee of the American Optometric Association.

fields.meaning: The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

example.value: doctorate
example.quote: shall be a graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.value: national_accreditor
example.quote: "recognized school or college of optometry" means a school or college approved by the American Optometric Association or a committee of the American Optometric Association.

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

example.quote: shall be a graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

example.quote: shall be a graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.value: embedded_in_credential
example.quote: shall be a graduate of a school or college of optometry recognized by the board

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)

example.value: at least 100 hours
example.quote: which internship includes at least one hundred (100) hours of supervised clinical training

fields.meaning: e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'

example.value: supervised clinical internship in examination, diagnosis, and treatment of conditions of the human eye and adnexa
example.quote: Served an internship program established by the board, supervised and certified by a board-certified ophthalmologist, which internship includes at least one hundred (100) hours of supervised clinical

fields.meaning: Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: National or international examination designated by the board
First section of the two-part examination.

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.

example.value: national or international, as designated by board regulation

fields.meaning: Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.

fields.meaning: Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

example.quote: the licensee has met continuing education requirements as may be prescribed by regulations of the board to ensure the continued protection of the public
The length of study shall be prescribed by the board but shall not exceed 25 hours in any calendar year.
All registered optometrists licensed in this state are required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of optometry.

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']

value: pain management and opioid use and addiction (at least 2 hours in the two years preceding renewal, unless licensee does not hold a DEA registration number)
example.quote: the two years preceding the application for renewal, the licensee has completed at least two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction, unless the licensee demonstrates to the

fields.meaning: Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: The board shall issue a license by credentials to an applicant who ... holds a current license to practice optometry in another state or territory of the United States or in a province of Canada that

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Applicant must: (1) be a graduate of a board-recognized optometry school; (2) pass the Alaska laws/regulations exam; (3) hold a current equivalent license from another US state/territory or Canadian province; (4) have previously passed the National Board of Examiners in Optometry exam; (5) have at least 3,120 hours of active clinical practice in the preceding 36 months; (6) have no disciplinary history; and (7) demonstrate adequate education in pain management and opioid use unless they lack a DEA registration number.

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: There is created the Board of Examiners in Optometry to regulate and control the practice of optometry and to protect and promote the public health, welfare, and safety.

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.

example.value: Connecticut Board of Examiners for Optometrists
example.quote: There shall be within the Department of Public Health a Connecticut Board of Examiners for Optometrists.

fields.meaning: Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

example.value: The board hears and decides matters concerning suspension or revocation of licensure, adjudicates complaints, and imposes sanctions; the Commissioner of Public Health makes and enforces regulations with advice and assistance from the board; the board may revoke or suspend licenses for cause.
example.quote: The Commissioner of Public Health, with advice and assistance from the board, may make and enforce such regulations, in accordance with chapter 54, as the commissioner deems necessary to maintain prop

fields.meaning: Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

example.value: National Board of Examiners in Optometry
example.quote: at some time in the past, received a license to practice optometry from another state or territory of the United States or from a province of Canada that required the person to have passed the Nationa

fields.meaning: Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

example.value: American Optometric Association
example.quote: "recognized school or college of optometry" means a school or college approved by the American Optometric Association or a committee of the American Optometric Association.

fields.meaning: Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.value: license
example.quote: A person may not practice, attempt to practice, or offer to practice optometry without first obtaining a license from the board.

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.value: license
example.quote: A person may not practice, attempt to practice, or offer to practice optometry without first obtaining a license from the board.

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: A person may not practice, attempt to practice, or offer to practice optometry without first obtaining a license from the board.

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: A person may not falsely personate a licensed optometrist, or buy, sell, or fraudulently obtain a license issued to another

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: A person may not practice, attempt to practice, or offer to practice optometry without first obtaining a license from the board.

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'

example.value: fraud_in_obtaining_license

fields.meaning: One-line plain-English description

example.value: Secured a license through deceit, fraud, or intentional misrepresentation.

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.

example.quote: By maintaining a surety bond in a form acceptable to the commissioner of insurance in the amounts set forth in subsection (1)(a) of this section

fields.meaning: Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?

example.quote: By maintaining commercial professional liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in this state in a minimum indemnity amount of one million dollars per incident

fields.meaning: Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?

example.quote: The owner and operator of a mobile optometric office shall register with the board.

fields.meaning: Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

example.value: board creation

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, or performance of preventive procedures related to diseases, disorders, or conditions of the human eyes or adjacent and associated structures, consistent with this chapter and regulations adopted by the board
example.quote: "optometry" means the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, or performance of preventive procedures related to diseases, disorders, or conditions of the human eyes or adjacent and associated

fields.meaning: High-level methods, e.g. ['medical','surgical','mechanical']

value: prescription and use of pharmaceutical agents including controlled substances
removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye and its appendages
example.quote: the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, or performance of preventive procedures related to diseases, disorders, or conditions of the human eyes or adjacent and associated structures

fields.meaning: Whether/how the profession may prescribe, administer, or dispense drugs.

example.value: A licensee may prescribe and use a pharmaceutical agent, including a controlled substance, in the practice of optometry if the pharmaceutical agent is used in a manner consistent with standards adopted by the board in regulation.

example.quote: authorizing an optometrist licensed under this chapter to delegate routine services of optometry to an agent of the optometrist

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly addresses or authorizes the delivery of optometric services via telemedicine.

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly addresses or regulates the operation of mobile optometric offices (vans, trailers, etc.).

fields.meaning: Whether the statute requires a special permit or registration to practice optometry at a patient's home residence.

example.quote: A patient's private home is not considered an established treatment site.

fields.meaning: Maximum number of offices a single optometrist or group may operate under the statute.

example.quote: No optometrist, and no two or more optometrists jointly, may have more than 11 offices.

example.quote: the optometrist or physician practicing as an ophthalmologist shall upon request of the patient provide to the patient a complete and accurate written prescription at no additional charge.

fields.meaning: Minimum number of years optometrists are required to retain patient records.

example.quote: An optometrist shall retain a patient's records for a minimum of seven years from the date he or she completes treatment of the patient.

fields.meaning: Whether the statute establishes or references a formal program for identifying, treating, and monitoring impaired optometrists.
